name: Tiger
description: The Bengal Tiger is India's apex predator and one of the most iconic big cats of the region.
behavior: Solitary and territorial; active at dawn and dusk.
safetyTips: Do not run. Back away slowly and keep visual contact.

name: Lion
description: The Asiatic Lion survives in limited habitats and is a powerful social predator.
behavior: Lives in prides; rests during the day and hunts in cooler hours.
safetyTips: Keep distance from pride zones and avoid approaching carcass sites.

name: Elephant
description: Indian Elephants are highly intelligent herd animals with strong social bonds.
behavior: Usually calm, but defensive around calves.
safetyTips: Never block herd movement and maintain wide distance.

name: Leopard
description: Leopards are stealthy and adaptable predators that can live near settlements.
habitat: Rocky hills, forest patches, agricultural edges
behavior: Mostly nocturnal and solitary; expert climbers.
safetyTips: Avoid walking alone at night near forest fringes.

name: Bear
description: Sloth bears are strong, short-sighted mammals that may charge when surprised.
behavior: Mainly nocturnal; forages for termites, fruit, and honey.
safetyTips: Make noise while moving through dense vegetation.

name: Gaur
description: Gaur are the largest wild cattle and can be dangerous if disturbed.
behavior: Herd-living and usually shy, but defensive when threatened.
safetyTips: Do not honk or approach gaur on roads.

name: Wild Boar
description: Wild boars are fast and aggressive with sharp tusks.
behavior: Often active at dawn and dusk; move in family groups.
safetyTips: If charged, move behind a tree or climb to safety.

name: Crocodile
description: Mugger crocodiles are ambush predators found in freshwater bodies.
behavior: Basks near banks and strikes quickly at close range.
safetyTips: Stay well away from water edges in known habitats.

name: Snake
description: Venomous snakes including king cobra may inhabit forest and farm edges.
behavior: Often avoids humans, but bites when cornered or stepped on.
safetyTips: Wear boots and never attempt to catch a snake.

name: Wolf
description: Indian wolves are alert, pack-oriented predators of open dry landscapes.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal; hunts in coordinated groups.
safetyTips: Secure livestock and avoid isolated night movement.

name: Deer
description: Spotted deer are common herbivores and key prey species in forest ecosystems.
behavior: Timid and alert; males can be aggressive in mating season.
safetyTips: Observe from distance and do not corner animals.

name: Peacock
description: Peacocks are vibrant ground birds known for display behavior in monsoon.
behavior: Territorial in breeding season; active in early morning.

name: Monkey
description: Macaques are intelligent primates that adapt quickly to human spaces.
behavior: Social troop-living behavior; food-conditioned groups may be aggressive.
safetyTips: Do not feed monkeys and keep food hidden.

name: Fox
description: Indian foxes are small canids adapted to open plains and scrub.
safetyTips: Do not attempt rescue; contact wildlife authorities if injured.

name: Eagle
description: Eagles are powerful raptors with excellent vision and soaring flight.
behavior: Daytime hunters; nests in high, undisturbed sites.
safetyTips: Stay clear of nesting zones and avoid throwing food scraps.
